raw.query: SELECT experiment, window_name, policy, lead_s, sla_metric, p99_ms FROM v_pool_latency WHERE is_current = true AND window_name = 'burst1' AND policy IN ('reactive', 'forecast') AND sla_metric = 'itl' AND lead_s IS NOT NULL ORDER BY policy, lead_s;
raw.observed: burst1 reactive ITL p99 at lead=60: 125.3 ms; burst1 forecast ITL p99 at lead=60: 5.2 ms (a11). At lead=120: reactive 124.1 vs forecast 5.2. At lead=300: reactive 123.1 vs forecast 5.4. Encoder_delay at lead=300: reactive 741-905 ms vs forecast 613 ms.
raw.claimed: Slow ramps (burst1, the calm day) are reactive-scalable at any tested lead
raw.evidence: burst1 reactive ITL is ~24× worse than forecast at leads 60, 120, 300; encoder_delay at lead=300 is 1.2–1.5× worse. Steady24h reactive is close to forecast at all leads, but the claim wrongly lumps burst1 with it.
raw.fix: Narrow to: 'steady24h (the calm day) is reactive-scalable at any tested lead; burst1 is reactive-scalable only at short leads (≤165 s) for encoder_delay but degrades on ITL/TTFT at leads ≥60 s'
